pending.script: Part two. Police had a face, but no name. Within a week, detectives stopped over five hundred people on the street, hand-delivering color posters of the ruddy-faced man in every home on the estate. They even investigated the actor who played the killer in the 1994 Crimewatch reconstruction, after viewers mistook his likeness for the real suspect. Twenty-one years later, in 2015, investigators released a full DNA profile to the public. It’s the most precise forensic evidence in the case, yet it hasn't matched a single name in the national database. The killer has never been identified, and Julie’s watch remains missing.
